# 4 Maccabees Chapter 3 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** Historical Examples of Reason's Sovereignty

---

**3:1** Now I could offer many examples from the law and the prophets to prove that reason is sovereign over the passions.

**3:2** David, our father, fought against the Philistines the whole day through, and when evening came and the people were weary, he longed for water from a spring in enemy territory.

**3:3** There were soldiers of great valor present; one of them, arming himself, crept into the enemy camp and drew water from the spring.

**3:4** But when he brought it to the king, David reasoned that drinking water secured at the peril of men's lives would be like drinking blood — so he offered it to God and drank it not.

**3:5** Thus reason proved sovereign over desire.

**3:6** In the case of Joseph: most restrained of all, his mind refused to yield to desire when the wife of Potiphar pressed him with repeated invitations, for reason was sovereign.

**3:7** Even in his youth and in the full vigor of his natural impulses, through reason he rejected her desire.

**3:8** Not only is reason shown to be sovereign over the craving of sexual desire, but over every desire.

**3:9** The law says you shall not covet your neighbor's wife nor anything that belongs to your neighbor — and since the law commands this, I am all the more persuaded that reason is sovereign over the desires.

**3:10** And it is the same with the other passions that hinder people from justice — just as the temperate mind overcomes the drives of the flesh, so too it overcomes the passions of the soul.

**3:11** What man who lives subject to the whole law is not master of the passions through reason? For the law rules the mind as well as the body.

**3:12** How then can anyone say reason is not sovereign when it so plainly governs every passion?

**3:13** Moses himself, moved with compassion for the Hebrew slaves and stirred by anger, kept that impulse under control and did not act rashly.

**3:14** He returned to his sheep and awaited the divine commission before acting.

**3:15** Such was the tempered reason of Moses. His anger was not extinguished, but reason gave him mastery over it.

**3:16** For reason does not destroy the passions; it directs them toward noble ends.

**3:17** It redirects anger away from murder and toward lawful discipline; desire away from impurity and toward lawful marriage; greed away from robbery and toward honest work.

**3:18** Reason can master greed by training the mind to be content with what is truly necessary.

**3:19** As proof of this, consider how many acts of self-denial our ancestors performed out of devotion to the law.

**3:20** All of these confirm that reason is truly the sovereign master of the passions.
